lines.en: Amara, you haven’t been here for years. Our city has changed a lot!

lines.en: It really has. They’ve built a new tower near the harbour.

lines.en: And the old market has become a modern food hall.

facts.label: Mudanças
facts.sub: Use has/have + particípio para mudanças com resultado no presente: has changed, have gone up, have built. Não use com tempo terminado.

facts.label: Mudou
facts.sub: Use has/have + particípio para uma mudança com resultado agora: The city has changed. They’ve built a new tower. A mudança ainda é visível no presente.

facts.label: Subiu / cresceu
facts.sub: Prices have gone up. The city has grown. Go vira gone no particípio, e grow vira grown. Esses verbos aparecem muito em conversas sobre mudanças.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “a cidade mudou” com o pretérito, mesmo se a mudança continua.
compare.us: Em inglês, use has/have + particípio para mudanças ligadas ao presente: The city has changed. Prices have gone up.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: This city has changed.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The city has changed uses the present perfect.
We say “The city has changed in 2020.”
items.why: With a finished time, use the past simple.

items.s: Prices have gone up means prices are higher now.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The city has changed uses the present perfect. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “The city has changed in 2020.” → Falso (With a finished time, use the past simple.)
Prices have gone up means prices are higher now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A changing city · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a bright morning in the centre of Vancouver. Max has just come back after three years abroad. He stands near the harbour and looks around. His friend Bill waits with two coffees. Many things look different now. Bill starts to explain what has changed.

“Max, you haven’t been here for years. Our city has changed a lot!” says Bill. “It really has. They’ve built a new tower near the harbour.” says Max. “And the old market has become a modern food hall.” says Bill.
